wl-001.label: Draft five candidate slogans for a new product from a two-line brief
wl-001.why: Creating new content from a prompt is generative AI — nothing is being analyzed, extracted or spoken.

wl-002.label: An assistant that checks inventory, files the reorder, and emails the supplier without step-by-step prompts
wl-002.why: Multi-step autonomous action with tool use is the agentic signature — histack's 'persistent assistant' vs 'one stateless response'.

wl-003.label: Determine who spoke when in a recorded meeting (speaker diarisation)
wl-003.why: Diarisation separates speakers within audio — a speech capability. Trap: it generates nothing, so it is never synthesis.

wl-004.label: A voice agent that must hold natural spoken back-and-forth conversations with minimal delay
wl-004.why: Verbatim Voice Live / gpt-realtime phrasing from the corpus — real-time audio in, audio out.

wl-005.label: Return bounding boxes around each vehicle in traffic-camera footage
wl-005.why: Object detection — bounding boxes per object — is computer vision, distinct from whole-image classification.

wl-006.label: Pull the invoice number, total, and due date out of thousands of scanned PDFs
wl-006.why: Extracting structured fields from documents and forms is the information-extraction workload — Content Understanding territory in Domain 2.

wl-007.label: Create a photorealistic hero image for a product page from a two-sentence text description of the item and its setting
wl-007.why: Creating an original picture from a written description is the image side of generative AI — there is no existing image being analyzed, which is what would make it computer vision.

wl-008.label: Produce a first draft of a product FAQ page from a bullet-point outline of talking points
wl-008.why: Turning a sparse outline into new prose is content creation from a prompt, the same capability as wl-001's slogans, just applied to a longer document.

wl-009.label: Answer a single one-off customer question in a chat window with one reply, with no follow-up steps or tools invoked
wl-009.why: One stateless response to one prompt is generative AI; the moment a system starts planning steps and calling tools on its own it crosses into agentic AI.

wl-010.label: A travel-booking assistant compares fares across three sites, holds a seat, and completes the purchase once the price target is hit, with no human confirming each step
wl-010.why: Comparing, deciding, and executing a purchase end to end with no per-step prompting is the agentic pattern, distinct from a chatbot that only replies.

wl-011.label: An IT-support assistant triages an incoming ticket, runs a diagnostic script against the affected server, and escalates to a human only if the automated fix fails
wl-011.why: Calling outside tools and then choosing the next step based on the result is what makes this agentic — distinct from a single generated response.

wl-012.label: A research assistant breaks a broad question into sub-questions, searches multiple sources for each, and stitches the findings into one final report
wl-012.why: Task planning that decomposes a goal into steps, executed end to end, is the exam's task-planning-plus-task-completion definition of agentic AI, not a single generated answer.

wl-013.label: Scan free-text support tickets and flag any phone numbers or email addresses they contain before the tickets are stored
wl-013.why: PII detection flags sensitive spans inside unstructured text — a text-analysis feature, distinct from information extraction's fixed fields pulled from forms and documents.

wl-014.label: A hotel chain wants the recurring subjects in guest reviews surfaced as a brief ranked set of terms, not a condensed prose recap
wl-014.why: Keyword extraction lists the salient terms; the classic trap is reaching for summarization instead, which would produce prose rather than a topic list.

wl-015.label: Identify every person name, organization, and location mentioned across a batch of news articles
wl-015.why: Named entity recognition classifies mentions inside running text into people, places and organizations — a text-analysis capability, not extraction against a fixed document schema.

wl-016.label: Condense a 40-page policy document into a three-paragraph overview that captures its key points
wl-016.why: Summarization compresses existing text into new but faithful prose — text analysis, not generative AI, because the output is grounded in and constrained by the source document.

wl-017.label: Transcribe a batch of uploaded interview recordings once they have all finished uploading, rather than as they are spoken
wl-017.why: Batch transcription processes pre-recorded audio asynchronously — still a speech capability, just the offline sibling of real-time recognition, not a text or extraction task.

wl-018.label: Produce natural-sounding narrated audio for an e-learning module from a written script
wl-018.why: Converting written text into spoken audio is text-to-speech synthesis — the output side of the speech workload, mirroring wl-004's audio-in/audio-out case.

wl-019.label: Verify that the person in front of a login camera is a live human being, not a printed photo or a video replay
wl-019.why: Face liveness detection defends against presentation attacks by analyzing the live camera image — a computer-vision security capability, distinct from face verification's identity match.

wl-020.label: Flag every frame of a building-site safety video in which a worker is not wearing a hard hat
wl-020.why: The deliverable is a judgment about what each frame shows, which is visual analysis; the same footage would shift to speech if the deliverable were the spoken transcript, and to information extraction if it were a schema of segments or chapters pulled from the whole video.

wl-021.label: Tag an uploaded photo with a single whole-image category such as 'beach' or 'city street', with no per-object locations needed
wl-021.why: Image classification assigns one label to the whole image, unlike wl-005's object detection, which returns per-object bounding boxes — both are computer vision, but distinct techniques.

wl-022.label: Run AI enrichment skills over thousands of scanned reports and images during indexing so content that was previously unsearchable becomes searchable
wl-022.why: This is knowledge mining — the exam's Azure AI Search definition of using AI skills to surface information from unstructured content into a search index.

wl-023.label: Return a schema-defined set of fields — call reason, resolution, and follow-up action — from a batch of recorded support calls
wl-023.why: Pulling a fixed business schema out of audio content is Content Understanding's structured extraction; the deliverable is defined fields, not a transcript, which is what would make it speech.

wl-024.label: Pull key-value pairs and table structure from a mixed batch of contracts, intake forms, and handwritten receipts using one reusable schema
wl-024.why: Structured field and table extraction across varied document types is document intelligence's layout/custom-model territory — the same workload as wl-006's invoices, applied to a broader document mix.

workload-sort.hint: Ask what the deliverable actually is: brand-new content from a prompt (generative), autonomous multi-step action with tools (agentic), a judgment or summary about existing text (text analysis), anything that touches spoken audio (speech), a judgment about an image or video frame (computer vision), or a fixed set of structured fields/an index pulled out of documents or mixed content (information extraction).
workload-sort.note: Several requests could sound like two workloads. The tie-break is always the deliverable: new content vs. an autonomous action vs. an analysis of existing text vs. audio in/out vs. a judgment about pixels vs. a structured field set.
workload-sort.zones[0].def: Creating new content — text, images, code, or audio — from a prompt, rather than analyzing or acting on content that already exists.
workload-sort.zones[1].def: Autonomously planning, using tools, and taking multi-step action toward a goal, going beyond a single stateless response.
workload-sort.zones[2].def: Analyzing written text to surface meaning already present in it — sentiment, key phrases, entities, PII, or a grounded summary — without generating new content.
workload-sort.zones[3].def: Converting between spoken audio and text, or working directly with audio streams — recognition, synthesis, translation, and diarization.
workload-sort.zones[4].def: Analyzing the visual content of images and video frames — classifying, detecting objects, verifying faces, or reading a scene.
workload-sort.zones[5].def: Pulling a fixed set of structured fields, or a searchable index, out of documents, forms, or mixed-modality content.
